newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 14.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The showdown between the government and judges, over the government's proposal to separate the new administrative court from the mainstream courts, has intensified with a gathering of more than 500 judges at the Criminal Court calling the prime minister a dictator. Despite strong opposition from judges, Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has reiterated that he wants the new court to remain with the Council of State, instead of the Justice Ministry which controls the mainstream courts. (THE NATION, BANGKOK POST)

- Road congestion will worsen over the next two years with the start of no fewer than 93 traffic-related projects, Deputy Interior Minister Chaipal Siriwat says. Among the jam-busting projects expected to create more jams is work on the subway, which begins in March. To help motorists avoid the worst of the congestion, leaflets detailing the construction projects and alternative routes will be distributed by a traffic agency in advance. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Constitution Drafting Assembly (CDA) has agreed to form five working committees and 76 provincial subcommittees to gather public opinion on the new constitution. CDA President Uthai Pimchaichon says it is agreed that the chairpersons of all committees will sit on the drafting panel to make sure that the new constitution corresponds with public opinion. (THE NATION)

- The Bank of Thailand (BOT), driven by a desire to turn local commercial banks into global corporations and a commitment to existing free-trade agreements, is set to raise foreign ownership restrictions in local banks from 25 percent to as high as 40 percent. However, the BOT will not change the foreign ownership limit on finance companies, which is currently pegged at 40 percent. (THE NATION, BUSINESS DAY)

- The government plans to spend nearly 71 billion baht developing the infrastructure and economy of the country's five southernmost provinces. A study of a proposed master plan for the development of the area is to be completed by the end of January. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Deputy Prime Minister Korn Dabbaransi is sending shock waves through the local oil refining and marketing industry with the assertion that oil firms should end their cross-shareholding in existing oil refineries. He says the directive will promote free competition in the Thai oil industry and encourage investment in new oil refineries around the country. (BANGKOK POST)
